 PFC Dividend 2026: Maharatna PSU declares 2nd interim dividend for FY27 with Q2 results; Check record date
 Written By Anubhav Maurya Published: 3:08 PM, Nov 4, 2026 | Updated: 3:08 PM, Nov 4, 2026 Maharatna PSU Power Finance Corporation (PFC) on Wednesday reported an 11.76 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in standalone profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 4,986.71 crore for the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27. Maharatna PSU Power Finance Corporation (PFC) on Wednesday reported an 11.76 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in standalone profit after tax. Image Credit: Canva Maharatna PSU Power Finance Corporation (PFC) on Wednesday reported an 11.76 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in standalone profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 4,986.71 crore for the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27, compared with Rs 4,460.68 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.
 The company's net profit exceeded the Zee Business estimate of Rs 4,938 crore.
 Total revenue from operations increased marginally by 0.26 per cent to Rs 14,793.20 crore in the July-September quarter, compared with Rs 14,755.50 crore in the year-ago period.
 The company's net interest income (NII) stood at Rs 5,122.11 crore during the quarter, falling short of the Zee Business estimate of Rs 5,204 crore.
 Profit before tax (PBT) increased 11.14 per cent YoY to Rs 6,157.13 crore in the reporting quarter, compared with Rs 5,539.89 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.
 Total expenses declined 3.42 per cent to Rs 8,815.98 crore during the July-September quarter, against Rs 9,128.52 crore in the year-ago period.
 PFC declares second interim dividend 
 The company's board declared a second interim dividend of Rs 4.10 per equity share for the financial year 2026-27. The dividend represents a payout of 41 per cent on the face value of Rs 10 per paid-up equity share, subject to deduction of tax at source (TDS).
 PFC said November 17, 2026, will be the record date for determining the eligibility of shareholders for payment of the second interim dividend for FY27.
 The record date is the date used by the company to identify shareholders eligible to receive the dividend.
 The company said the payment of the second interim dividend will be made on or before December 4, 2026.
 PFC dividend record date and payment 
 Shareholders holding eligible PFC equity shares as of the record date of November 17, 2026, will be entitled to receive the second interim dividend, subject to applicable conditions.
 The dividend will be paid at Rs 4.10 per equity share, with the amount subject to deduction of TDS. PFC has set December 4, 2026, as the latest date for payment of the second interim dividend for FY27.
 PFC Dividend History 
 Power Finance Corporation (PFC) has consistently rewarded its shareholders through dividends. The company declared an interim dividend of Rs 3.90 per share in August 2026, following a dividend of Rs 3.95 per share in July 2026.
 Earlier in 2026, it announced interim dividends of Rs 3.25 per share in March and Rs 4 per share in February.
 In November 2025, PFC declared an interim dividend of Rs 3.65 per share, followed by Rs 3.70 per share in August 2025 and a dividend of Rs 2.05 per share in June 2025.
 During the financial year 2024-25, the company announced interim dividends of Rs 3.50 per share in March, February and November 2024, and Rs 3.25 per share in August 2024.
 It had also declared a dividend of Rs 2.50 per share in July 2024 and interim dividends of Rs 3.50 and Rs 3 per share in February and March 2024, respectively.
 PFC H1 results 
 For the first half of the financial year 2026-27, PFC reported a net profit of Rs 9,732.11 crore, up 8.58 per cent from Rs 8,963.44 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.
 Total revenue from operations increased 0.90 per cent YoY to Rs 28,786.33 crore during the April-September period, compared with Rs 28,528.92 crore a year ago.
 The company's total income rose 1.53 per cent to Rs 28,968.01 crore during the first half of the financial year.
 Total expenses declined 3.33 per cent to Rs 16,897.79 crore in the April-September period.
 Profit before tax increased 9.20 per cent YoY to Rs 12,070.22 crore, compared with Rs 11,053.05 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.
 Total tax expense rose 11.89 per cent to Rs 2,338.11 crore during the first half of FY27.
